subject: Doubt with JAGS and Node inconsistent with parents

messages.author: 49df7864c81ad508
messages.subject: Doubt with JAGS and Node inconsistent with parents
parts:
Hello:

I am using camtrapR to analyse data from 32 camera traps distributed in a heterogeneous farmland, in order to observe the change in biodiversity affected by different environments. In order to do so, I created a community model and used the environment factor as a fixed variable to observe how different species were affected by this factor. All worked properly until the time of fitting the model, when R gave me an error. Specifically R told me that:

Error in rjags::jags.model(file = object@modelFile, data = object@data, : Error in node y[1,1,2] Node inconsistent with parents

I am quite new to JAGS and Bayesian Statistics overall, so I really didn't know what I was doing wrong. I tried checking the vignette on the matter at hand to see if my data structure was faulty but I can't find the error. At last, I saw that when I created my detection history matrix, I set the output as "count" instead of "binary". Changing it to "binary" allowed me to fit the model and continue with my analysis. My question is more of a curious one, as I do not really understand why the detection histories with counts is not usable for this kind of model. Is  there any way to use the "count detection history matrix" to build a community model of this nature? Or is it statisticallly nonsensical? I checked the pdf file describing the package and I found no function regarding this option so I suspect it might be the latter. Anyway, I felt I had to leave this comment for anyone having the same error and if anyone could enlighten me when it comes to my doubt. 

           Kind regards:

                    Unai

messages.subject: Re: Doubt with JAGS and Node inconsistent with parents
parts:
Hi Unai, 

the issue might arise when creating the detection histories matrix. 

Try to change the line 

day1 = "station",

with 

day1="survey",

Hope this can help.

Stef
